hero.title: Taking FIRST to the capitol.
hero.subtitle: GEarheads doesn't just compete in FIRST — we fight for it. Three years running, we've walked the halls of the Wisconsin Capitol, sat with federal legislators in D.C., and pushed for the policy changes that get robotics into more classrooms.

impact.label: What we secured
impact.text: The DPI Robotics League Bill passed — $500,000 a year in state funding for K–12 robotics across Wisconsin. Seven students drove the effort, meeting more than 75 legislators over three years to get it done.

whyWeAdvocate.heading: Why we advocate
paragraphs: GEarheads competes because FIRST works — it teaches you to design under constraints, test against data, and pitch ideas to people with real authority. But none of that happens if a school can't afford a team. Registration fees, field sets, materials — that's the wall. Our advocacy exists to knock it down.
We don't show up at the Capitol asking for favors. We bring evidence — participation numbers, outcome data, and a student who can tell a legislator exactly what FIRST did for them. Hard to wave off.

One visit doesn't change much. Three years of showing up, same faces, updated data, does. That's how meetings became trust, and trust became a bill — $500,000 a year, every year, for students who've never heard of GEarheads.

Advocacy also sharpens what FIRST teaches. A policy brief is a design problem. Winning over a skeptical legislator is a communication problem. Tracking a bill through committee is project management. We do it because it works, and because it makes us better engineers.

milestones.label:
WI Capitol
Advocacy Day
milestones.summary: Three consecutive years of student voices in the Wisconsin State Capitol.
milestones.detail: FIRST Advocacy Day sends student teams into the Wisconsin Capitol to make the case for FIRST funding, in person. GEarheads has shown up three years running — one of the most consistent student voices in the state. We write testimony, rehearse with our mentors, and meet our district reps and committee chairs. Over three years we've talked with more than 75 legislators. Year one, they're curious. Year two, they remember us. Year three, they sponsor the bill.
highlights: Three years running at the Wisconsin Capitol
Talked with 75+ state legislators
Wrote testimony and policy briefs each year
Met district reps and committee chairs
Built real legislative credibility over time

milestones.label:
FIRST WI
Student Board
milestones.summary: A formal seat on the FIRST Wisconsin Student Board of Directors.
milestones.detail: GEarheads holds a seat on the FIRST Wisconsin Student Board of Directors, the student group that helps set the state's advocacy priorities. It's real work — meetings and planning all season — and it keeps a suburban, mid-size-district voice like Brookfield's in the room for statewide decisions. It also connects upward into the national FIRST network, so a meeting in Madison can shape testimony in Washington.
highlights: Seat on the FIRST Wisconsin Student Board
Shapes state advocacy and programming
Represents Elmbrook's perspective statewide
Meets and plans all season
Bridges team-level and state-level leadership

milestones.label:
Governor's Cup
Washington D.C.
milestones.summary: An hour with Governor Evers and his policy staff in Washington D.C.
milestones.detail: The FIRST Governor's Cup trip brings a handful of student teams to D.C. to advocate for STEM funding federally. GEarheads landed a meeting with Governor Tony Evers that ran over an hour, with his spouse and two policy staff in the room. Students laid out Wisconsin's robotics funding gaps and raised the DPI proposal that later became law. The Governor's team asked real questions and let the meeting run long. We also met federal legislators on Capitol Hill.
highlights: 1+ hour with Gov. Evers and two policy staff
Presented K–12 robotics funding proposals
Meeting ran long — it landed
Also met federal legislators on Capitol Hill
Linked the state push to federal STEM policy

milestones.label:
K–12 DPI
Funding Push
milestones.summary: Expanding Wisconsin's robotics funding from grades 6–12 to K–12.
milestones.detail: One thing we pushed for: expanding Wisconsin's DPI robotics funding from grades 6–12 down to K–12, so elementary FLL programs get the same support as FTC and FRC. The earlier kids meet FIRST, the more likely they stick with it. Cutting funding off at grade 6 left the biggest on-ramp unpaid for, dependent on parent fundraising. We brought FLL participation data to show funding the whole pipeline pays off. Now a fifth grader has a real path from a funded FLL team to FTC to a college engineering program.
highlights: Pushed DPI eligibility from 6–12 to K–12
Framed the FLL gap as a pipeline problem
Backed it with FIRST Wisconsin enrollment data
Linked FLL investment to FTC/FRC outcomes
Covers the full FIRST pipeline, not just competition

milestones.label:
Chips &
Sciences Act
milestones.summary: One of five teams nationally to advocate for the Chips & Sciences Act.
milestones.detail: GEarheads was one of five robotics teams nationwide picked to advocate around the CHIPS and Science Act, the roughly $280 billion federal law funding semiconductor manufacturing, research, and STEM workforce development. Our job: convince federal legislators that FIRST robotics is exactly the applied STEM experience the Act is meant to support. We met with six federal legislators. Being chosen said something about the credibility we'd built nationally — these conversations move faster and cut deeper than state-level ones.
highlights: One of 5 robotics teams picked nationally
Met with 6 federal legislators on Capitol Hill
Advocated for K–12 STEM pipeline provisions
Engaged with the Act's education funding
Signals national credibility in the FIRST policy world

milestones.label:
DPI Robotics
League Bill
milestones.summary: The bill passed. $500,000 in annual state funding secured.
milestones.detail: Three years of state advocacy led here: the DPI Robotics League Bill passed, directing $500,000 a year in permanent state funding to K–12 robotics through the Department of Public Instruction. Not a grant — programs can budget around it every year. Seven GEarheads students carried the push: testifying, meeting sponsors, tracking committee votes, keeping relationships alive across sessions. It covers registration fees, field sets, and materials — the exact costs that price teams out.
highlights: $500,000 a year, signed into law
7 students led the legislative push
Permanent funding, not a one-time grant
Covers fees, field sets, and materials
Three years of work, one signed bill
